checkpoint_review: I agree with the Router's assessment of all testable checkpoints. The primary wombat exhibits correct head shape, nose texture, fur quality, and body proportions. The Router correctly marked 'Short powerful limbs...' and 'Low center of gravity...' as untestable due to straw occlusion; while the general stance is visible, specific anatomical details like claws and foot contact points are genuinely obscured. I also agree that the vestigial tail checkpoint is passed by absence of a prominent tail.
artifact_review: The Router identified two artifacts: texture anomaly (reddish leaves) and blur (secondary wombat). I agree with the severity of the texture anomaly (2/5); the reddish objects on the right lack coherent geometry and appear fused with the wall, a clear generation defect. However, I disagree with the Router's classification of the secondary wombat's blur as an artifact (severity 1). Upon visual inspection, the blur on the left subject is consistent with photographic depth-of-field (bokeh), where the background/secondary subject is naturally out of focus relative to the sharp foreground subject. There are no structural deformities or melting in the secondary subject, only optical defocus. Therefore, this should not be penalized as an AI artifact. No new artifacts were found by experts or myself beyond the confirmed texture issue on the right.
alignment_reasoning: 7/7 testable checkpoints passed with high confidence. Expert evidence supports taxonomic accuracy. Two checkpoints correctly deemed untestable due to occlusion. Primary subject anatomy is robust and conforms strictly to wombat morphology.
artifact_reasoning: Router correctly identified texture fusion on the right edge (severity 2). Router incorrectly flagged secondary subject blur as an artifact; visual analysis confirms this is natural depth-of-field, not a generation failure. Adjusted artifact score upward to reflect only the genuine texture defect.
key_defects: Reddish leaf-like objects on the right exhibit texture fusion and lack physical depth against the corrugated wall.
